title: Matrix Calculation in the Exceptional Unitary Case
body_html:
Matrix Calculation in the Exceptional Unitary Case

In the exceptional case, \(D/k\) is ramified quadratic, the dual pair is an equal-rank unitary pair, and the residual regular semisimple element \(\lambda^\circ\) has rank \(n-1\). After base change, the residual space is two copies of \(n\times n\) matrices. The Galois action exchanges the two components of \(\bar w=(A,B)\), forcing \(A\) and \(B\) to have rank \(n-1\).

The stabilizer of \(\bar w\) in \(S_\lambda\) equals the subgroup acting trivially on \(\operatorname{Im}\lambda^\circ\). Hence \[ X_{\lambda,\lambda'}\simeq S_\lambda/S_{\bar w}, \] and a character occurs in the residual function space exactly when it is trivial on \(S_{\bar w}\).
proof_html: The proof replaces the full general linear stabilizer by the special-linear stabilizer of \(\lambda^\circ\), where the relevant orbit is free. Galois invariance then descends the orbit statement to the original group. The equality \(S_{\bar w}=S_\lambda|_{\operatorname{Im}\lambda^\circ=\operatorname{id}}\) follows from \(\operatorname{Im}\bar w^*=\operatorname{Im}\lambda^\circ\).
